main_topics.reason: The user came with nail changes and finger pain and spent most turns learning what it might be and whether it is serious.
The user described morning stiffness, finger swelling and pain in the opening turns and asked about relief.
The user raised nail changes at the start and asked later what could help the nail they hide.
The user asked whether to go back to the dermatologist and how referral works through a health plan, then planned to request it.
The user asked in one exchange whether waiting could cause permanent damage.
The user asked what happens at the rheumatology visit because they dislike not knowing.
The user asked whether a blood test confirms the diagnosis, in one exchange.
The user asked what they can take for the pain and mentioned occasional use of a common analgesic.
The user asked what could be done for the nails and whether treating arthritis would help them.
The user said they were worried and scared at the start and during the discussion of permanent damage.
The user noted once that their dermatologist never raised this.

output.summary: A user with long-standing psoriasis described nail pitting, a lifting nail, finger pain with morning stiffness and sausage-like swelling. The bot explained these may point to psoriatic arthritis, advised a rheumatology evaluation within weeks and explained the referral route via the Brazilian health plan, what the visit involves and the diagnostic approach. The user said they felt better with a plan and would ask for the referral that week.
